Article Title: Amid delimitation Bill buzz, NCP-SP MPs meet PM Modi
Article Text:
Sule and her colleagues said their meeting with Modi was focused on development issues concerning Maharashtra

(With inputs from Anurag Bende in Pune)

NEW DELHI: Eight Lok Sabha MPs of NCP(SP) led by Supriya Sule met PM Narendra Modi on Monday amid buzz that govt is eyeing their support for its constitution amendment bill for delimitation and indications from the governing alliance that it has two-thirds support in Parliament required for the legislation’s passage.Sule and her colleagues said their meeting with Modi was focused on development issues concerning Maharashtra, but, coming as it did days after the party’s patriarch Sharad Pawar met PM ostensibly over similar matters, political circles were agog with speculation that the regional party was coming closer to BJP over its centrepiece bill.Last month, Sule had said her party may consider backing delimitation if all states see an equal 50% rise in their Lok Sabha seats — something which, interestingly, forms the core of the bill — while insisting that NCP(SP) will take a final decision in consultation with its opposition allies.Meanwhile, Congress is upset over its ally NCP(SP)’S talks with the top brass of BJP at the Centre and in the state.“When the opposition has cornered Prime Minister Modi and home minister Shah over recent police violence during CJP [Cockroach Janta Party] protest at Jantar Mantar, such meetings of opposition members give the wrong message. Ultimately, the leadership of that party will have to decide which path to follow,” a senior Congress member said.Stressing that there was no discussion about the delimitation bill during the meeting, Shirur NCP (SP) MP Amol Kolhe said, “The purpose of the meeting was to seek intervention of the Prime Minister in some of the key issues such as agrarian crisis in the state, long pending Pune-Nashik railway project and infrastructure problems faced by industries.”Former CM and senior Congress functionary Prithviraj Chavan said, “I do not know the agenda of such meetings, but apart from such scheduled meetings, some secret meetings also keep happening. Some members of the parties in the govt have told me that they will be attempting to split NCP (SP). I do not know if the meeting had anything to do with it.”NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar met Modi last month. A meeting between Supriya and Shah followed.As these meetings were happening in Delhi, the party’s former state president Jayant Patil held closed-door talks with CM Devendra Fadnavis in the latter’s Mumbai residence. NCP seniors Praful Patel and Sunil Tatkare were also present there.
Article Summary: Eight Lok Sabha MPs of NCP(SP) led by Supriya Sule met PM Narendra Modi on Monday. Meeting comes amid buzz that govt is eyeing their support for its constitution amendment bill for delimitation. Congress is upset over its ally NCP (SP)’S talks with the top brass of BJP at the Centre and in the state.

Article Title: 2 held in J&K for spreading radical, anti-national content
Article Text:
Police have arrested the accused, Tariq Ahmad Sofi, employed with wildlife department in Ganderbal.

SRINAGAR: J&K police’s counter-intelligence wing arrested two individuals on Monday for allegedly disseminating anti-national content, radical narratives, and extremist viewpoints through social media platforms.The arrests followed raids on Saturday across five locations in Baramulla, Bandipora, Anantnag, and Shopian districts, where digital devices were seized in a case registered under UAPA. Equipped with incriminating evidence, police arrested Mehran Qazi from Anantnag and Babar Hamid from Sopore.
Article Summary: Arrests followed raids on Saturday across five locations in Baramulla, Bandipora, Anantnag, and Shopian districts. Digital devices were seized in a case registered under UAPA. Equipped with incriminating evidence, police arrested Mehran Qazi and Babar Hamid.

Article Title: NCP (SP) MPs’ meeting with PM Modi upsets Congress
Article Text:
NCP (SP) MPs met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Monday

Pune:





The meeting of eight NCP (SP) MPs with Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Delhi on Monday reignited speculations over Sharad Pawar ’s party joining hands with NDA, while its ally Congress was upset over parleys of the outfit’s members with the top brass of BJP at the Centre and the state.“When the opposition has cornered Prime Minister Modi and home Minister Shah over recent police violence during CJP (Cockroach Janta Party)’s protest at Jantar Mantar, such meetings of opposition members give the wrong message. Ultimately, the leadership of that party will have to decide on which path to follow,” a senior Congress member said.All eight MPs of Sharad Pawar’s party, led by Supriya Sule , met Prime Minister Modi in New Delhi. The meeting was held against the background of NCP (SP) indicating its conditional support to the delimitation bill, expected to be tabled in Parliament. The MPs of Sharad Pawar’s party claimed that they met the Prime Minister to raise issues pertaining to their respective constituencies.Stressing that there was no discussion about the delimitation bill during the meeting, Shirur NCP (SP) MP Amol Kolhe said, “The purpose of the meeting was to seek intervention of the Prime Minister in some of the key issues such as agrarian crisis in the state, long pending Pune-Nashik railway project and infrastructure problems faced by industries.”After Monday’s meeting of NCP MPs with Prime Minister Modi, former chief minister and senior Congress member Prithviraj Chavan said, “I do not know the agenda of such meetings, but apart from such scheduled meetings, some secret meetings also keep happening. Some members of the parties in the govt have told me that they will be attempting to split NCP (SP). I do not know if the meeting had anything to do with it.”Before the meeting of eight Lok Sabha MPs with the Prime Minister, NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar met Modi last month. A meeting between Supriya and Shah followed.While these meetings were happening in Delhi, the party’s former state president Jayant Patil held a closed-door meeting with chief minister Devendra Fadnavis in the latter’s Mumbai residence. NCP seniors Praful Patel and Sunil Tatkare were also present there.Senior Congress member Chavan had earlier claimed that there was growing unease among the NCP (SP) members following six MPs of Shiv Sena (UBT) switching over to Eknath Shinde’s Shiv Sena.
Article Summary: All eight MPs of Sharad Pawar’s party, led by Supriya Sule, met Prime Minister Modi in New Delhi. Meeting was held against background of NCP (SP) indicating its conditional support to the delimitation bill, expected to be tabled in Parliament.

Article Title: ‘No mandate to sing Tamil Thai Vazhthu last’: Centre tells HC
Article Text:
Chennai:





The Union govt on Monday told the Madras high court that its latest notification on singing Vande Mataram at govt functions does not mandate that the Tamil Thai Vaazhthu should be sung at the end of such events.Additional solicitor-general A R L Sundaresan, appearing for the Centre, made the submission before the first bench comprising Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G Arul Murugan while hearing a PIL filed by Chennai-based Ananya Radhakrishnan.The petitioner had sought directions to the authorities to ensure that govt functions in Tamil Nadu begin with the Tamil Thai Vaazhthu.According to the petition, it has been the practice in Tamil Nadu for several years to begin govt functions with the Tamil Thai Vaazhthu and conclude them with national anthem. The petitioner alleged that this practice was being diluted by singing Vande Mataram and national anthem before the Tamil Thai Vaazhthu.She challenged a Jan 28 circular issued by the Union home ministry, contending that the Tamil Thai Vaazhthu was not merely ceremonial but represented the sentiments, culture and identity of the Tamil people.The petitioner sought quashing of the circular and a direction to the state govt to issue appropriate administrative instructions to ensure that govt functions begin with the Tamil Thai Vazhthu.When the petition came up for hearing before the first bench, Sundaresan submitted that the home ministry had since issued a fresh notification and, therefore, the petition had become infructuous. He said the notification provided for Vande Mataram to be sung first, followed by the National Anthem, but did not mandate that the Tamil Thai Vazhthu should be sung last.The bench adjourned the matter to next week.
Article Summary: The Union govt told the Madras high court that its latest notification on singing Vande Mataram at govt functions does not mandate that the Tamil Thai Vaazhthu should be sung at the end of such events. The bench adjourned the matter to next week.

Article Title: Justice D Krishnakumar assumes office as State Law Commission chairman in TN
Article Text:
Justice (retired) D Krishnakumar





CHENNAI: Former Madras high court judge Justice (retired) D Krishnakumar on Monday assumed office as the chairman of the State Law Commission.He was acting chief justice of the Madras high court before being appointed as the chief justice of Manipur high court. He attained superannuation on May 21, 2025.The state govt reconstituted the law commission through a govt order dated Aug 7 and appointed Justice (retired) Krishnakumar as the chairman of the commission.Former Madras high court judge RMT Teekaa Raman, former additional chief secretary TK Ramachandran and former law department secretary A Arunagiri were appointed as full-time members. Former district judges P Mohan Doss and R Govindarajan were appointed as part-time members, while an officer in the cadre of secretary, law department, will serve as the full-time member secretary.The commission will suggest suitable modifications or amendments to plug loopholes in existing laws and recommend social and economic legislative measures. It will also suggest ways and means for interstate relations and Centre-state relations and make recommendations for judicial and administrative reforms aimed at improving and expediting procedures.
Article Summary: Justice (retired) D Krishnakumar assumed office as the chairman of the State Law Commission. He was acting chief justice of the Madras high court before being appointed as the chief Justice of Manipur high court. The commission will suggest suitable modifications or amendments to plug loopholes in existing laws.

Article Title: Truck driver dies in road accident near Salem
Article Text: SALEM: A driver died in an accident involving a truck, a pickup van and a bus near Mecheri in Salem district on Wednesday. More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident.According to the Mecheri police, a TNSTC bus carrying 51 passengers was heading to Karur from Mettur when a speeding pickup van attempted to overtake it. “The pickup van collided head-on with a truck coming from the opposite direction,” said an officer at the Mecheri police station. The truck grazed the bus, shattering its windows and injuring more than 10 passengers seated near the windows.Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. The injured were rushed to govt hospitals in Mettur and Omalur.Fire service personnel, assisted by Mecheri police and residents, worked to move the damaged truck and pickup van to the roadside. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.The Mecheri police registered a case.
Article Summary: More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident. Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.

Article Title: Arrest blunder in Nithin Raj death case: Kerala HC slams govt to delay in action against cop
Article Text:
R L Nithin Raj

Kochi:





The high court on Monday criticised the state govt for the delay in suspending crime branch DSP Sudheer Kallan for his alleged failure to follow the mandatory arrest procedure while arresting Dr M K Ram, an accused in the death of BDS student Nithin Raj in Kannur, which resulted in his release by court.A bench of Justice A Badharudeen further directed the state police chief to pass an expeditious order within a week on the preliminary inquiry report against the erring officer. The court issued the order in a petition concerning the release of Ram by the jurisdictional court, citing procedural error in his arrest. While considering the case, the court asked why the officer had not been suspended from service pending inquiry and whether officials in higher ranks wanted to save him.On Monday, the govt placed on record an order issued by the additional chief secretary of the home department, which found a serious lapse on the part of the officer. However, no immediate action had been taken by the competent authority. Instead, the govt order stated that a panel of competent officers would be appointed to conduct the inquiry. Going through the preliminary inquiry report of the Wayanad SP, referred to in the govt order, the court remarked that coercive action was required against the erring officer.Accordingly, the bench directed the state police chief to pass an appropriate order and constitute a competent panel of officers to conduct the inquiry.Ram was arrested on July 20 by a crime branch team from Kodagu in Karnataka in connection with the death of Nithin, a first-year BDS student of Anjarakandy Dental College, Kannur. It was alleged that Ram, along with other faculty members, had harassed the student. However, the special court in Thalassery set aside the arrest after finding that the investigating officer had failed to inform Ram of the grounds of arrest, as mandatorily required by law.The preliminary inquiry report on the incident revealed that although Ram is a native of Andhra Pradesh, the notice was issued in Malayalam and the investigating officer had failed to ensure that its contents were explained to him, adversely affecting the prosecution. During the hearing, the bench orally asked why the govt was delaying action against him when the preliminary inquiry report had revealed such a serious lapse.Accordingly, the court adjourned the case to Aug 17 for the govt’s reply.
Article Summary: Dr M K Ram is an accused in the death of BDS student Nithin Raj in Kannur. A special court in Thalassery set aside the arrest after finding that the investigating officer had failed to inform Ram of the grounds of arrest.
